why_trail.why: This repo has docs/agents/ (ORCHESTRATOR_CONTEXT.md only) and NO docs/architecture/ - so it is itself the degraded common case the g3 run must exercise, and the dead-path prose claiming a skill-source repo has no docs/agents/ overlay is falsified by the repo I am standing in. The gate is deletion PLUS run; pre-registration is committed at 0119fa4/1662b90 and must not be rewritten. Highest risk is T4: 'no docs/agents/ overlay at all' occurs at offsets 262 and 2330 in tasks.context.imperative and only the second may go.

Block (a) deleted by offset-bounded raw-text slice (wc -w = 86 words). T4 did NOT fire: the overlay phrase count went 2 -> 1 and the surviving occurrence is asserted to sit inside the substitute-and-record sentence. docs/agents/engine-config.json still appears in the imperative (the intake sentence names it), so the context_refs stop condition is not triggered. UNANTICIPATED CONFLICT, resolved and named as a deviation: test_context_manifest.py pinned 'sanctioned degradation' and 'do NOT create the overlay file' as prose sentinels - both phrases OF THE DELETED BLOCK. Its sentinels were re-pointed at surviving degraded-mode prose, intent and count unchanged. That file is outside the handoff's allowed scope; the edit is forced by the assigned deletion and is reported as a deviation.

Block (b) deleted the same offset-bounded way; wc -w over both deleted blocks reports 86 + 86 = 172, matching the handoff's corrected count exactly and derived from a command rather than asserted. A SECOND out-of-scope sentinel surfaced: test_map_contract_wiring.py also pinned 'sanctioned degradation'. Same minimal intent-preserving fix, same named deviation. A corpus-wide sweep for the deleted phrases found two remaining live references, both flagged rather than edited: scripts/verify_context_declaration.py's docstring (illustrative, not enforcing) and docs/superpowers/drills/dogfood-context-paths-absent.md (a historical run record that would be falsified by editing).

T3's plan-side retarget was genuinely still outstanding, contradicting the handoff's expectation that g2 had done it. The evidence is a command over git history rather than a reading of the current file alone, because 'was it already done' is a question about history. The edit is 4 words replacing 4 - the smallest change that names the resolved input instead of an unnamed 'current map' - and it makes the plan step consistent with prose already in the same imperative ('the map inventory the context step resolved'). This does NOT move the anchor: the plan step still fires at authoring time, which is exactly why T3/T5 predict no ordering change.

The run is a real result in both directions. The contract REPORTS rather than passing silently: it refused the advance, named the missing receipt, named exactly what a degraded verdict still owed, and accepted only a discharge carrying a hash-pinned substitute plus the unmapped gap plus an escalation. And the deletion changed nothing mechanical: both checklists carry config_ref docs/agents/engine-config.json, that file does not exist, and the engine degraded it silently and correctly with no prose anywhere telling it to. The T5-relevant finding is a NEGATIVE with evidence: grep for map_before_src in map_orient.py returns nothing - the gate observes the RECEIPT's content, never tool ordering - so a run may still read fifty source files, then discharge orientation, then advance context. Better positioned, not enforcing.

Two of five outcomes are honest negatives or non-results, and they are recorded as such rather than rounded to HELD: T3's mapped-repo clause is UNTESTED (no instrument), and T5 is NOT DETERMINABLE (a single scripted drive by the anchor's own author is not a behavioural sample). The pre-registration anticipated exactly this for T5 and asked for the gap to be named. The one forward-looking obligation this produces: POST must be designed to distinguish 'insufficient' from 'irrelevant', which needs runs under BOTH anchors - a POST that samples only the new anchor will return 'unchanged' and be unable to say which it saw.

The store has no 'confirmed' standing (#342), so a tripwire that held and one never checked look identical in the store. That is exactly why each observed-behavior carries a specific quoted observation and the pre-registration SHA: the citation is doing the work the missing standing cannot. Episode -005 deliberately records NOT DETERMINABLE plus the forward measurement requirement rather than a verdict.

The snapshot's baseline commit is a8d9467, g3's own starting point, NOT the pre-registration 0119fa4 - measuring from 0119fa4 would show the spine GROWING, because g2 landed several hundred words of verify-frame prose in between, and would silently attribute g2's addition to g3's deletion. The 172-deleted vs 168-corpus-moved gap is stated explicitly for the same reason: a successor that finds arithmetic that does not close will assume a miscount rather than the +4 retarget.
